PHW R Markdown output formats

Source: R/rmarkdown.R
phw_formats.Rd

Branded versions of the standard R Markdown formats. Use them in the YAML header of an .Rmd file:

Usage

phw_html_document(
  ...,
  toc = TRUE,
  number_sections = FALSE,
  fig_width = 7.5,
  fig_height = 4.5,
  style_plots = TRUE,
  palette = NULL
)

phw_word_document(
  ...,
  toc = FALSE,
  number_sections = FALSE,
  fig_width = 6.3,
  fig_height = 3.9,
  style_plots = TRUE,
  palette = NULL
)

phw_pdf_document(
  ...,
  toc = FALSE,
  number_sections = TRUE,
  fig_width = 6.3,
  fig_height = 3.9,
  cover = TRUE,
  team = NULL,
  style_plots = TRUE,
  palette = NULL
)

Arguments

...

Passed to the underlying rmarkdown format.

toc

Include a table of contents?

number_sections

Number the headings (1, 1.1, ...) like PHW reports?

fig_width, fig_height

Default figure size in inches.

style_plots

Apply use_phw_ggplot() and use_phw_flextable() while knitting?

palette

Qualitative palette for the whole document, e.g. "accessible". NULL uses phw_default_palette(). The palette is put back as it was when the render finishes.

cover

Draw the full-page gradient cover when the document has a title?

team

Team line on the cover, e.g. "Communicable Disease Surveillance Centre".

Value

An R Markdown output format.

Details

output: phwstyle::phw_html_document

  • phw_html_document(): Bootstrap 5 with phw_bs_theme(), the gradient header band with the white logo, and PHW styles for the title, headings, tables and captions. Works offline because the fonts are embedded.

  • phw_word_document(): uses a reference document with Ubuntu, navy headings, booktabs tables, a gradient band and logo header, and a "Page x of y" footer.

  • phw_pdf_document(): XeLaTeX with Ubuntu, a full-page gradient cover, a running header band and a branded footer.

All three call use_phw_ggplot() (and use_phw_flextable() when flextable is installed) before knitting, so charts and tables match without extra code: don't repeat those calls in the document, and add theme_phw() or a PHW scale to a plot only to change something for that plot. If one of these steps fails, the document still renders and a warning says what was left unstyled.

Accessible colours. palette = "accessible" switches every chart, table and widget in the document to the colour-blind safe palette. To make both versions of a report, leave the document alone and set it when you render:

word <- "phwstyle::phw_word_document"
rmarkdown::render("report.Rmd", word, output_file = "report.docx")
rmarkdown::render("report.Rmd", word, output_file = "report-accessible.docx",
                  output_options = list(palette = "accessible"))

Or set it for good in the YAML header:

output:
  phwstyle::phw_word_document:
    palette: accessible

See phw_default_palette() for the other ways to switch. For larger text and thicker lines as well, call use_phw_ggplot(accessible = TRUE) in the setup chunk.

Examples

# Use a format in the YAML header of an .Rmd file:
#
#   output: phwstyle::phw_word_document
#
# or give it to rmarkdown::render(). Making the format object is quick:
if (requireNamespace("rmarkdown", quietly = TRUE)) {
  fmt <- phw_word_document(toc = TRUE)
}
# \donttest{
# Render one document twice: default colours, then accessible colours
if (requireNamespace("rmarkdown", quietly = TRUE) && rmarkdown::pandoc_available() &&
    interactive()) {
  rmd <- file.path(tempdir(), "report.Rmd")
  writeLines(c("---", "title: Example report", "---", "",
               "```{r, echo = FALSE}",
               "library(ggplot2)",
               "ggplot(mpg, aes(class, fill = drv)) + geom_bar()",
               "```"), rmd)
  rmarkdown::render(rmd, phw_word_document(), output_file = "report.docx")
  rmarkdown::render(rmd, phw_word_document(palette = "accessible"),
                    output_file = "report-accessible.docx")
}
# }
